title: Safety precautions: the pistol
subtitle: When to make it safe, and the five steps

lines: This episode covers safety precautions with the semi-automatic pistol.
Carrying out your safety precautions means you unload the firearm, or make it safe.

scenes.heading: Never pass on a loaded firearm
bullets: Never hand over a loaded firearm
First carry out your safety precautions
Unload it, or make it safe
lines: One should never accept a loaded firearm from another person.
Nor should you hand over a loaded firearm to another person.
Before you hand your firearm over, you should first carry out your safety precautions.
This means that you are going to unload the firearm, or make the firearm safe.

scenes.caption: Handing over a semi-automatic pistol
lines: When handing over a semi-automatic pistol, the magazine should be removed and the slide should be locked back.
The muzzle should not point at anybody during the exchange.
If you are handing over a revolver, the cylinder should be left open during the exchange.

scenes.heading: When to carry out safety precautions
lines: There are three times when you carry out safety precautions.

lines.text: One. When receiving a firearm.
Two. Before handing over a firearm.
Three. Before cleaning a firearm.

scenes.caption: Identify a safe direction, then point the firearm in it
lines: Safety precautions should be carried out in the following manner.
Step one. Identify a safe direction.
Step two. Point the firearm in a safe direction.
Keep your finger off the trigger and alongside the frame.

scenes.heading: Steps 3 and 4

lines.text: Step three. Maintain a safe direction while performing the following steps.
For the semi-automatic pistol, remove the magazine.
Step four. Pull back the slide.
If there was a round in the chamber, it would have been ejected by pulling the slide to the rear.
Now look into the chamber, and look down the magazine-well, the part that the magazine fits into.
This makes sure there is no ammunition in the firearm.

lines: You look to ensure that no round has been left in the firearm due to a faulty or broken extractor.

scenes.caption: Checking the chamber and magazine-well
lines: Here is that check in the book's photo.
Keep the muzzle in a safe direction, with your finger off the trigger, while you check inside the chamber and down the magazine-well.

lines.text: Back on our pistol, the magazine is out.
And the slide is still to the rear.
Step five. You now release the slide back under control to the forward position.
You will notice that the hammer has been left in the rearward position.
You need to lower the hammer under control.

scenes.heading: Don't dry fire
bullets: Don't squeeze the trigger and dry fire
Over time, it can damage the firing pin

lines.text: Even though the firearm is now unloaded, it is still best not to squeeze the trigger and dry fire the handgun.
Dry firing can, over time, damage the firing pin.
It is also a bad habit.

lines: Sooner or later, you are bound to have an accidental discharge when you think the handgun is unloaded.

scenes.heading: The five steps: semi-automatic pistol
bullets: Point it there, finger off the trigger
Keep a safe direction; remove the magazine
Pull back slide; check chamber and magazine-well
Release slide under control; lower the hammer
lines: Let's put the five steps together.

lines.text: One. Identify a safe direction.
Two. Point the firearm in a safe direction, finger off the trigger and alongside the frame.
Three. Maintain a safe direction, and remove the magazine.
Four. Pull back the slide, and look into the chamber and down the magazine-well.
Five. Release the slide under control, and lower the hammer under control.

scenes.question: When should safety precautions be carried out?
options: When receiving, before handing over, before cleaning
lines: The exam asks this one.
When should safety precautions be carried out?
reveal: When receiving a firearm, before handing over a firearm, and before cleaning a firearm.

scenes.question: Why look into the chamber and down the magazine-well?
options: A round may be left by a faulty or broken extractor
lines: After pulling back the slide, why do you look into the chamber and down the magazine-well?
reveal: To ensure that no round has been left in the firearm due to a faulty or broken extractor.

points: Never accept or hand over a loaded firearm
Slide forward under control, lower the hammer
lines: So, never accept or hand over a loaded firearm.
Carry out safety precautions when receiving, before handing over, and before cleaning a firearm.
Remove the magazine, pull back the slide, and check the chamber and magazine-well.
Release the slide under control, and lower the hammer under control.
And don't dry fire the handgun.
